quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane while you are riding in traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve into other lanes if needed to avoid hitting the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Stay in your lane.
Flash your lights to scare the animal away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Try to avoid hitting an animal if you can do so safely. In traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into another lane can cause you to hit another vehicle. A small animal is less dangerous than a crash.

questions.question: When riding, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders when looking through a turn.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes when looking through a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes when looking through a turn.
questions.explanation: When making a turn, look to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: How can you regain control if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Release the rear brake.
Keep using the rear brake.
Swerve the bike toward safer areas.
Accelerate while keeping the brake engaged.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the rear brake.
questions.explanation: To regain control of a locked rear wheel, you must release the brake. If the rear brake locks on a surface with good grip, you can keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: Why should you not move to the far side of your lane when being passed?

options.text: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too early.
You may block another vehicle from passing you.
The near side of the lane is safer.
You will feel the wind from the passing vehicle more.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Do not ride on the far side of your lane when being passed. This may encourage the other driver to return to your lane before it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Why should you avoid changing gears on railroad tracks?

options.text: Your motorcycle may stall.
You might go too fast.
Other drivers may not expect you to change gears.
The uneven surface makes gear changes harder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may stall.
questions.explanation: Do not shift gears when crossing railroad tracks. Your motorcycle might stall while you are on the tracks.

questions.question: To stop quickly, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes.
Use the rear brake firmly and gradually increase front brake pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: Stay in the center of your lane.
Stay on the right side of your lane.
Move onto the shoulder.
Turn on your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind or by oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane. Getting closer to the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders be placed when riding in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
Just behind the lead rider.
At the back of the group.
Anywhere in the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front of the group, just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders behind them can watch over them.

questions.question: What helps you ride safely on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Using only the front brake.
Using both brakes.
Using the center lane.
Keeping or increasing your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, use both brakes, and avoid sudden moves. Avoid the center of the lane and follow tire tracks from cars instead. Watch for hazards like oil spots and loose gravel.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes.
Do not brake; downshift instead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed and avoid sudden moves. Use both brakes if you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: When loading cargo onto a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Put lighter items near the front.
Try not to place items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag. Place the load over or in front of the rear axle. Putting the load behind the rear axle will make the motorcycle harder to control.

questions.question: When planning a long group ride, which idea should you NOT use?

options.text: Plan travel segments based on the least experienced rider.
Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
Put inexperienced riders behind the leaders.
Ride in a staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
questions.explanation: Plan route length based on the least experienced rider's ability. Take regular breaks to reduce tired riders. Put inexperienced riders behind the leader so experienced riders can watch them. Ride in a staggered formation.

questions.question: When a vehicle passes you on your left, what should you do?

options.text: Move as far right as possible to help them pass.
Move to the shoulder to help them pass.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride in the left part of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on either side of your lane is dangerous. The side closest to the passing vehicle risks a crash. The farthest side might tempt them to merge back too soon.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What is the best lane position when traveling through a curve?

options.text: The far left part of the lane.
Always the center part of the lane.
The far right part of the lane.
It changes based on how the road curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: It changes based on how the road curves.
questions.explanation: No single lane position works for all curves. The best position may change even within one curve. Every curve is different. Road geometry, traffic, and road conditions may change as you go through the curve.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Squeeze the front brake hard to prevent tire lock.
Use only the rear brake.
Use only one brake at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes when riding on slippery surfaces. Squeeze the front brake lever slowly to avoid locking the front wheel. Use gentle pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: When making normal stops, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both the front and rear brakes.
Switch between the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping, even for regular stops that are not emergencies.

questions.question: When packing a load on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Put heavier items toward the front.
Put heavier items toward the rear.
Mount loads behind the rear axle.
Store lighter items in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items toward the front.
questions.explanation: Position loads with heavier items toward the front. Place the load over or in front of the rear axle. Pack lighter items behind you.

questions.question: How does a motorcycle's stopping distance compare to a car's stopping distance?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need a little longer to stop.
Motorcycles need longer to stop.
Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, motorcycles and cars have nearly the same stopping distance. However, on slippery surfaces, it is much harder for motorcycles to stop quickly.

questions.question: When stopping behind a vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop far back, then slowly move up.
Stay well behind the vehicle.
Stop right behind the vehicle quickly.
Stay about four car lengths back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay well behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when both vehicles are stopped. The vehicle could back up suddenly. You may also need space to move away if another vehicle hits you from behind.
